workflow: A container update invokes user-defined value-conversion code while preparing an element assignment.
The conversion callback re-enters the container and clears or shrinks its backing storage.
The original update resumes with a stale index and storage pointer without revalidating the container’s current bounds or allocation.
It writes through the invalidated storage, causing a null dereference or use-after-free instead of returning a recoverable bounds error.
summary: Reentrant mutation invalidates container storage during an ongoing update
decision_reason: The failure workflow materially matches reentrant cleanup or callback code mutating a container while the original operation still holds and uses its storage address; the differing conversion and assignment details do not change the core invalidation sequence.
